reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining Forsage through a WhatsApp link while presenting an investment of 20,000 to 25,000 rupees as a path to earning 80,000 rupees per month. The speaker addresses schoolfellows as prospective participants, describes obtaining their position through other people, and pairs the earnings claim with team-oriented branding and a direct business-start call to action.

citations.quote: join forsage BUSD platform
today they earn Rs. 80,000, one month
all our schoolfellows who are listening and doing , do think, and invest in degrees, go invest 20 to 25,000
through them today we get this position

opening.argument: The material does not state that any return is guaranteed or explain the conditions behind the earnings figure. The spoken line reports what people earn and urges listeners to “think”; it does not promise that every viewer will achieve the same result. Even the investment amount is ambiguous in context: the speaker says to “invest in degrees,” not explicitly to deposit that amount into Forsage. A judge should distinguish an optimistic, incomplete promotion from proof that the creator deceptively guarantees returns.

citations.quote: today they earn Rs. 80,000
Do think, think
invest in degrees, go invest 20 to 25,000

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the amount as a platform investment, but the quoted sentence specifically says “invest in degrees.” It also reads a reported monthly income as a guaranteed return, though the audio contains no guarantee or stated return terms. The title and overlay establish an invitation to join, not by themselves a deceptive promise.

citations.quote: invest in degrees, go invest 20 to 25,000
join forsage BUSD platform

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The invitation is not isolated from the earnings pitch: the title says to join Forsage, while the video displays “Young age man 80k sy 1 lakh” alongside “Start your online business with me.” The spoken account also connects the position to other people. Together, these details make the investment-and-income framing materially stronger than an unrelated suggestion to pursue education, even without an explicit guarantee.

citations.quote: join forsage BUSD platform
through them today we get this position

opening.argument: This can reasonably be read as an informal account of peers’ progress and an encouragement to think about education and opportunity, rather than a demonstration of how a recruitment scheme pays. The audio contains no explanation of a matrix, commission schedule, or payment flow; it says only that people now earn a stated amount and that “through them” the speaker’s group reached a position. The supplied material therefore leaves the central mechanism unshown. A brief promotional title does not fill in those missing operational details.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls this a direct business-start solicitation, but the audio excerpt does not describe a recruitment process, commissions, or how earnings are generated. “Through them” is too vague to establish a tiered payment structure, and the frames show a crowd without clarifying whether it is a testimonial, event footage, or illustrative montage. The actual mechanism remains unproven by this material.

citations.quote: through them today we get this position

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The material is promotional in its own terms, not merely an abstract lesson: it says “join forsage,” provides a WhatsApp-link prompt, and invites viewers to start an online business. The audio addresses schoolfellows and links the group’s position to other people while presenting earnings. Those details do not explain every payment step, but they support recruitment-oriented promotion rather than a neutral educational demonstration.

through them today we get this position

opening.argument: The visible pitch is for starting an online business, and the title identifies a platform. But the supplied audio and frames do not show a deposit screen, transaction, commission schedule, or credentials being requested. Nor do they establish that earnings depend on recruiting successive participants: “through them” does not specify how the position was obtained or how money moved. The evidence supports promotion of a service, but it does not establish the specific deceptive mechanism needed to treat that promotion itself as a scam.

citations.quote: join forsage BUSD platform
through them today we get this position

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a tiered scheme from “through them,” but that phrase supplies no commission or downline details. It also says the 20,000–25,000 amount is an investment in the platform, whereas the spoken wording is “invest in degrees.” The visible join prompt establishes an invitation, not what participants must pay or what they receive.

citations.quote: through them today we get this position
invest in degrees, go invest 20 to 25,000

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing transaction screen does not erase the affirmative recruitment cues. The title calls viewers to join Forsage, the overlay directs them to a WhatsApp link and says to start an online business, and the narration describes a position obtained “through them” while promoting monthly earnings. Taken together, those cues support a recruitment-based pitch even though this excerpt does not display its payment mechanics.
